entries.hint: A thorny shrub famous for sweet-smelling flowers in many colors
entries.fact: The fruit of the rose, called a hip, is rich in vitamin C.

entries.hint: A spring bulb flower shaped like a cup
entries.fact: Tulips grow from bulbs planted in autumn and bloom in spring.

entries.hint: A feathery green plant that unrolls from curled-up fiddleheads and makes spores instead of seeds
entries.fact: Ferns were growing on Earth long before flowering plants appeared.

entries.hint: A tiny package holding a baby plant and its first food
entries.fact: Some lotus seeds have sprouted after hundreds of years.

entries.hint: The flat green part of a plant that catches sunlight
entries.fact: Leaves make food for the plant using sunlight, air and water.

entries.hint: The part of a plant that grows underground to drink water
entries.fact: Roots also anchor a plant so wind does not tip it over.

entries.hint: A giant grass with hollow stems that can grow very tall, very fast
entries.fact: Giant moso bamboo can grow about a meter in one day.

entries.hint: A spiky succulent whose thick leaves hold a soothing gel
entries.fact: Aloe stores water in its thick leaves to get through dry weather.

entries.hint: Pink spring flowers from trees that people celebrate with festivals in Japan
entries.fact: In Japan, people gather under the blooming trees for picnics called hanami.

entries.hint: The nut that grows into a mighty oak tree
entries.fact: Jays bury acorns and don't always dig them up, so some grow into new oaks.

entries.hint: A colorful leaf-like part of a flower that attracts visitors
entries.fact: Petal colors help bees and butterflies find flowers.

entries.hint: Sweet liquid that flowers offer to bees
entries.fact: Bees turn nectar into honey back at their hive.

entries.hint: A meat-eating plant with hinged leaves that snap shut
entries.fact: It closes after two touches in quick succession, which helps it ignore raindrops.

entries.hint: An African tree with a thick bottle-shaped trunk
entries.fact: Big baobab trunks can store over 100,000 liters of water.

entries.hint: A desert plant that looks just like a pebble
entries.fact: Lithops are called living stones because they blend in with the pebbles around them.

entries.hint: Yellow dust that bees carry from flower to flower
entries.fact: Pollen grains have shapes so distinct that scientists can identify plants from them.

entries.hint: A baby plant that has just sprouted
entries.fact: A seedling uses the food stored in its seed until its leaves can make more.

entries.hint: A grassy field full of wildflowers
entries.fact: A meadow can be home to many kinds of flowers and insects.

entries.hint: A small bog plant with sticky glistening drops that trap insects
entries.fact: Its sticky drops look like morning dew, which gives the plant its name.

entries.hint: A climbing vine with an intricate, star-shaped bloom
entries.fact: Its complex blooms have many frilly filaments in the center.

entries.hint: A pale white woodland plant with no green at all
entries.fact: It has no chlorophyll and gets its food through fungi in the soil.

entries.hint: What a seed does when it wakes up and starts to grow
entries.fact: Most seeds germinate when they get enough water and warmth.

entries.hint: A plant that comes back year after year
entries.fact: Perennials rest in winter and sprout again in spring.

entries.hint: Describes trees that drop their leaves in autumn
entries.fact: Deciduous trees shed leaves to save energy through the winter.

entries.hint: A Namib desert plant that grows just two leaves, ever
entries.fact: Its two leaves keep growing for centuries, splitting into ribbons.

entries.hint: A silvery spiky plant that grows on high Hawaiian volcanoes
entries.fact: It grows for many years, blooms once, then sets seed.

entries.hint: A tree whose peeling bark reveals streaks of green, orange and purple
entries.fact: Its bark sheds in strips, showing fresh colorful layers beneath.

entries.hint: The green stuff in leaves that captures sunlight
entries.fact: Chlorophyll gives leaves their green color.

entries.hint: How plants use sunlight, water and air to make their own food
entries.fact: Plants release oxygen as part of photosynthesis.

entries.hint: When pollen moves from one flower to another so seeds can form
entries.fact: Bees, butterflies, birds and wind all help with pollination.
